subject: Outputs: ephemeral vs persisted PII - confirmation & next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Outputs: ephemeral vs persisted PII - confirmation & next steps

Hi Sarah / ClearSight compliance team —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Per our conversation, below is a concise recap of how Redwood treats PII in prompts and generated outputs, plus the concrete next steps we discussed. Let me know if you want anything tightened for your procurement review.

Summary (short):
- Prompt text: by default, hosted API retains raw prompt text in ephemeral request logs for up to 7 days for debugging metrics. For customers that enable analytics/logging we persist anonymized request logs up to 90 days.
- Generated outputs: not persisted by default. Outputs are persisted only when a customer opts in to "session logging" or enables usage analytics. Persistent output retention defaults to 90 days for hosted customers; Dedicated and Private can set to 0 days (no persistence).
- Embeddings & derived artifacts: stored only if you call the embeddings endpoint with storage enabled. We never index embeddings into shared catalogs unless explicitly opted-in.
- Redaction & tooling: SDK-side redaction helpers available (client-side). Server-side redaction templates available as a managed option. We support regex-based and field-based redaction before any persistent storage.
- Data residency & encryption: persisted logs are stored in the region you select (you chose us-east1). All at-rest data is encrypted with AES-256; customer-managed keys via KMS available for Dedicated & Private.
- Audit & deletion: we provide an API to purge logs and can provide deletion confirmation; audit logs (who/when) are retained for 1 year by default for compliance review.

What we agreed on / proposed options for ClearSight:
1) Default hosted posture: 7-day ephemeral debugging logs; analytics opt-in to 90-day analytics retention.
2) Strict PII configuration (recommended for PHI-like workflows): disable server-side persistence (0-day retention), require client-side redaction, and enable KMS-managed keys.
3) Rollout steps: sign DPA addendum; confirm residence region (us-east1); DocuSign for the DPA + SOC2 attestation provided.

Attachments: DataProcessingAddendum_v2.docx (DPA v2), SOC2_Attestation_Redwood_2026.pdf, call-recording-20270303.mp3 (recording of today's demo).

Next steps / asks for ClearSight:
- Sarah: confirm whether you prefer the Strict PII configuration (0-day persistence) or the Default hosted posture.
- Our side: we will attach DPA and SOC2 (attached) and prepare a DocuSign flow to lock in retention terms.
- Proposed follow-up: 30-minute alignment call — Mon, Mar 8, 2027 10:00am PT (we're flexible).

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Grace —

Thanks for the clear recap — a few clarifying questions from our compliance team before we proceed to DPA/DocuSign:
1) When you say "prompt text retained in ephemeral request logs for up to 7 days," is the full plaintext stored or are there hashed/sampled records? We need clarity because some of our prompts include patient identifiers.
2) If we pick "Strict PII" (0-day persistence), does that also prevent temporary KV cache from being written to disk? Our security team asks specifically about any on-disk artifacts that might contain raw prompts.
3) Is there an API-level mechanism we can call to request immediate purge for a given trace id and receive a deletion confirmation?

Also, please confirm whether embeddings generated by Redwood are ever retained by default for fine-tuning or model improvement. We do not want our embeddings used in model training unless explicitly contracted.

Appreciate the quick answers. If it helps, we can take your proposed follow-up on Mon 3/8.

Best,
Sarah Morrison
Director, Security & Compliance | ClearSight Analytics
sarah.morrison@clearsight.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Outputs: ephemeral vs persisted PII - confirmation & next steps

Hi Sarah — quick answers inline to keep this actionable.

> 1) Full plaintext or hashed/sampled records for the 7-day ephemeral logs?
We store full request/response payloads in ephemeral logs for hosted debugging. Ephemeral logs are retained in-memory and in short-term object storage for durability; default retention is 7 days. For customers who have "no persistence" configured (Strict PII), we disable writing those request logs to persistent object storage and keep only in-memory traces that are dropped on restart — effectively 0-days on-disk.

> 2) Does 0-day persistence prevent KV cache from being written to disk?
Yes — with Strict PII enabled we do not write KV caches to customer-visible persistent volumes. There is still transient in-memory KV caching required for inference; those caches are not flushed to disk in Strict mode.

> 3) Is there an API to request immediate purge with confirmation?
Yes — we offer an admin API to trigger immediate purge for request logs/outputs and return a purge transaction id. For enterprise contracts we can extend this with an attestation report (signed) upon deletion; add-on item in the DPA if you need formal signed confirmation.

> Embeddings retention and training usage?
Embeddings are never used in Redwood-managed model training by default. Embeddings are persisted only when you explicitly call embeddings+store APIs or opt into embedding analytics. We will add a line in the DPA that explicitly prohibits Redwood from using customer embeddings for model improvement unless separately contracted in writing.

Operational note: for Dedicated/Private deployments we can enforce the Strict PII posture by configuration and KMS key control; for hosted customers we have an opt-in flag and a contractual addendum (the DPA) to lock retention at 0 days.

Happy to walk through any of this on the 3/8 call; I can be available 10:00am PT. Monica/Rishi: can you confirm operational runbook availability if ClearSight wants a delete attestation?

Thanks —
